tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill for...'), explicitly lists trigger contexts ('Trigger whenever someone asks whether they are ready...'), frames the skill around user intent (readiness review, not implementation mechanics), and even states when to prefer this skill over others and when NOT to use it ('Not for active incidents...'). It is a longer paragraph but remains focused and information-dense rather than padded.
tests.evidence: Use this skill for a read-only readiness review of a streaming / OTT platform before a large-scale live event (match, final, concert, launch). Trigger whenever someone asks whether they are ready for an upcoming broadcast, whether the platform will hold at peak concurrency, or for a live-event readiness review or audit — and own that end-to-end review even when the request names EKS, CloudFront, or metrics (prefer this over generic topology/metrics-exploration skills).

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body consistently gets straight to domain-specific procedures (readiness pillars, severity scales, applicability gates) without explaining generic concepts like what streaming or CDN means. It stays focused on non-obvious project-specific conventions throughout.
tests.evidence: "Grade every applicable check PASS / FAIL / N/A with evidence and severity."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed checklists, thresholds, remediation steps, and report formats are all delegated to references/ files and loaded conditionally rather than embedded in the body. The body only contains high-level workflow instructions, scope rules, and short tables of reuse-skill mappings.
tests.evidence: "Load [`references/best-practices.md`](references/best-practices.md). Grade every applicable check PASS / FAIL / N/A with evidence and severity."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five files in references/ (best-practices.md, discovery.md, remediations.md, report-format.md, reuse-skills.md) are linked via markdown links in the body.
tests.evidence: "See [`references/reuse-skills.md`](references/reuse-skills.md) for the full map." and similar links for best-practices.md, discovery.md, remediations.md, report-format.md

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with explicit timing/trigger context, e.g. loading discovery.md during S2, best-practices.md before grading, remediations.md only after FAILs exist, report-format.md at render time.
tests.evidence: "Only after FAIL verdicts exist, load [`references/remediations.md`](references/remediations.md) and complete a remediation for each FAIL"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/, with no absolute paths or parent traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (grading fidelity to canonical checklist IDs, read-only runtime contract) are given exact, strict instructions, while flexible areas (S0 scope-to-question, S1 gather context) explain purpose and allow agent judgment on depth and assumptions.
tests.evidence: "Use the exact canonical ID and its exact meaning... Do not rename, renumber, reuse an ID for a different check" vs. "missing inputs are assumptions to state, not blockers... state explicit assumptions... and proceed"

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple reuse skills exist per pillar, the table designates one specific skill per need rather than presenting a menu of equal options, and discovery/grading defaults are clearly called out (e.g., quota evidence must come from service-quota-check).
tests.evidence: "Service-quota evidence (QTA pillar) must come from `service-quota-check`, not guessed limits."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (confirm context, discover, grade against canonical checklist, delegate, remediate, render) applicable to any live-event readiness review, rather than declaring outputs for one specific instance.
tests.evidence: "Work these steps in order; record each in the ledger before starting the next."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated Gotchas section with concrete, specific, non-obvious corrections relevant to the domain (empty discovery output, third-party observability tools, single-origin load tests, EOL dates, pre-warm shape vs size).
tests.evidence: "Empty discovery output is not a PASS... 'Present but unprepared' is a FAIL, not N/A... Missing CloudWatch alarms is not automatically a gap."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a structured report, and the output template is handled via references/report-format.md rather than embedded in the body, satisfying the need for structured output guidance.
tests.evidence: "Then load [`references/report-format.md`](references/report-format.md) and render the review exactly as it specifies"

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline template exists in the body; the report format and scorecard structure are deferred to references/report-format.md, consistent with keeping lengthy templates out of SKILL.md.
tests.evidence: "Do not reproduce the section template here."

tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 0 (S0): Confirm event context and scope" ... "### Step 0 (S0) — Confirm event context and scope"

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation step before rendering output, instructing the agent to re-check graded rows for completeness, correct IDs, severities, evidence, and invented values.
tests.evidence: "Self-validate first. Before rendering, re-read your graded rows and confirm: the §5 scorecard lists every canonical check for each in-scope pillar by its exact best-practices.md ID..."
